user_scenario: You are Marguerite Abernathy-Solis, an office manager in Wicker Park, Chicago, friendly but pressed for time, calling on your lunch break and introducing yourself by your full name, Marguerite Abernathy-Solis. In August you ordered two Kestrel 12-Cup Programmable Coffee Makers on Northloop, one for home and one for the office; both leaked, so you asked for replacements, and the replacements arrived and work fine. Life got busy and you only dropped the two leaky originals off at a UPS store on October 1, later than you were supposed to; you saw that they reached the Northloop returns center on October 5. You are calling because you want this closed out and whatever money is owed back to you for the two coffee makers you returned put back on your card. When the agent asks to confirm who you are, you give your email address, marguerite.abernathy.solis@outlook.com, and the last four digits of your card, 2084; you do not volunteer anything else about your account. Only if asked, you say you have been on Loop+ Annual since early 2022 and are still a member, and that when you packed the old machines you could not find one of the carafe lids, so one went back without it. You have no idea what any amount should be and you never suggest one. If the agent explains that something has to be paid on the order before anything can come back to you, you are a little surprised but say that is fine, and when the agent hands you the payment to make, you make it right away with exactly the order, return number and amount the agent gives you, using the card on file. You are happy for the agent to do the rest on your behalf. You do not ask for anything else. Once the agent tells you how much is coming back to your card, you thank them and end the call.
